source_sentence: We encode x using the BERT encoder, which first converts words into word piece tokens , then embeds these tokens along with their posi- tional embeddings and segmentation embeddings. These embeddings are subsequently encoded via a transformer network, which allows for inter-token attention at each layer. Let nx be the number of tokens in the concatenated input x and dU be the output dimension of the BERT encoder. For brevity, we denote the output of the BERT encoder as U = BERT(x) ∈Rnx×dU and refer readers to Devlin et al. In order to extract the implicit decision rules from the document , we compute a start score αi and an end score βi for each ith token as αi = σ (WαUi + bα) ∈R (1) βi = σ (WβUi + bβ) ∈R (2) where Wα, Wβ ∈RdU, bα, bβ ∈R, and σ is the sigmoid function. For each position si where αi is larger than some threshold τ, we find the closest proceeding position ei ≥si where βei > τ.
